Method of Attack: Encrypts files using AES encryption via PowerShell script
Steals information including screenshots, passwords, contacts, system audio recordings, and data from installed programs (Skype, Steam, Chrome, Thunderbird, Minecraft, TeamSpeak, Firefox)
Deletes files without backup including stolen folders and desktop files
Deletes Shadow Volume Copies to prevent file recovery
Displays ransom lock screen demanding $50 USD in bitcoins
Impacted Systems: Windows computers (implied by use of PowerShell, %LocalAppData% paths, Shadow Volume Copies)
Installed programs: Skype, Steam, Chrome, Thunderbird, Minecraft, TeamSpeak, Firefox
Attack Vector: Malware creation kit allowing criminals to create malware
Indicators of Compromise: Encrypted files appended with .crypt extension (e.g., test.jpg.crypt)
Ransom demand for $50 USD in bitcoins
